reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 4 close, data fresh: SPX 7,688.62 is only 1.99% off its 120-day high and 5.03% above its 200-day average, while the AI complex is deep in the drawdown — SMH $504.27 in Zone 2, down 24.94% from its high, and NVDA $200.13 on the Zone 1 floor. VIX 16.61 has fallen from a 21.15 five-day high, HY OAS 3.40 is calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: The Probe stance is wrong if HY OAS breaks above 4% with VIX above 25, or if SMH closes below $470 and NVDA below $175 on expanding volume — either voids the zone thesis and turns the correction into a deeper drawdown regime.

ladder.response: Hold the probe, do not average down into the break — the next zone down is the escalation, and sizing waits for the new zone print and a fresh tally.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA closes below $175 (Zone 2 floor)

ladder.response: Treat as the bull trap: do not chase, do not add on the bounce — wait for the failure-zone retest verdict and the second-low test before any further entry.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750–7,820 failure zone, or SMH into 580–600, and stalls or fails

ladder.response: Stand down — no new probes, ladder void, regime-break conditions met; reassess from cash.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Promote Probe to Add per the Tranche A ladder — the capitulation confirmation the zone print alone does not give.
ladder.trigger: SMH volume climax with intraday reversal AND VIX rollover confirmed (tally 4 of 4)

ladder.response: Regime break: the correction thesis is void, stance moves to Watch from cash until a new episode state prints.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day average of 7,320.35

reaction.trapRisk: SPX rose 1.58% on the day and VIX fell 20.26%, which looks like a pivot — but SMH fell 2.75% on the same day and NVDA 3.17%, so the bounce is in the index, not the AI complex. Chasing this first bounce into the 7,750–7,820 failure zone risks buying the trap; entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict or a second low that holds, not for the first green day.

strategyPosture: Probe. SMH has printed Zone 2 and NVDA sits on the Zone 1 floor with credit calm, but only 2 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals have confirmed — probe-sized starter only, no chasing the index bounce, and no full Add until the tally completes.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read holds while credit stays loose: the weakness is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, and the index is not confirming a broad rollover. But the divergence itself is real and worth tracking — if lending standards tighten or HY OAS breaks 4%, the rotation read fails and this becomes a rollover. The gap is the signal, not the noise.
themes.dataAnchor: SPX closed 7,688.62, down 1.99% from its 120-day trailing high of 7,844.52 and just 0.06% below its 50-day average. The Mag 7 average sits 14.07% below 52-week highs versus SPY at 1.9%, a 12.17-point divergence gap — MSFT is only 0.6% off its high while GOOGL is 29.3% off its. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad correction — AI names down 20–45% in a month — yet the index itself is only 1.99% off its 120-day high and rose 1.58% on the day. The market believes leadership is rotating, not that the market is breaking.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS rising toward 40% voids the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: The election is a real catalyst, not pure sentiment — the Texas outcome changes the merchant-power math, and a KeyBanc downgrade is a genuine re-rating input. But the price move (38.9% off the high) has overshot the revenue print (+19.1%) and insider buying says the trough is being bought, not abandoned. This is a screened candidate to verify, not a chase — the thesis needs confirming before any sizing.
themes.dataAnchor: VST closed at $120.29, down 15.82% on the day, down 26.79% over one month and 38.9% from its 52-week high, RSI 32.5. VRT fell 15.88% on the day and is 21.58% off over one month; GEV fell 12.29% and ETN 11.80% on the day. Against that, VST revenue is still growing 19.1% year over year, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and ETN revenue is growing 22.2% year over year.
themes.label: AI Power Trade Unwind
themes.narrative: The US midterm election outcome killed the AI power trade — merchant power generators sold off as the market priced policy risk into the nuclear and power buildout, with Vistra plunging 13.5% on a KeyBanc downgrade.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above $120 with insider follow-through, or a second downgrade wave, decides whether this is a trough or a re-rating.

themes.counterRead: Prices say the AI cycle is over; revenue says it is still compounding at 55–131%. The gap is the opportunity — but only 2 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals have confirmed (zone occupancy and credit calm), with no volume climax and no VIX rollover yet. A zone print alone is not a bottom call; it is a probe condition, not an all-clear.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH closed $504.27, inside Zone 2 ($470–505), down 24.94% from its 120-day high and 11.53% below its 50-day average. NVDA closed $200.13, on the Zone 1 floor ($200–210), down 17.77% from its high with RSI 34.5. Revenue says the opposite of the price: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year, AVGO 55%, LRCX 131.3%, all with recovery-confirmed inflections, and NVDA carries conviction score 83.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure in the Buy Zone
themes.narrative: The AI bubble is bursting — semiconductors are in free fall, SMH is down 11.17% in five days, and the complex is being abandoned.
themes.watchFor: SMH volume climax with intraday reversal and VIX rolling over from its 21.15 five-day high complete the capitulation tally.

themes.counterRead: The derating is a multiple story, not a cash story — DDOG's 80% gross margin and 29.2% free-cash-flow margin are intact while the price is 37% off its high. If revenue holds, price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions and this is the setup. If growth decelerates, the multiple is right and the dislocation is a value trap.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is $188.72, down 37.2% from its high with RSI 28.7, yet revenue is growing 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow at a 29.2% margin. NET is $266.58, down 28% from its high with RSI 34.1 and revenue growing 34.7% year over year. NOW is $108.81, down 38.1% from its high with RSI 30.7; SNOW is $290.60, down 24.4% with RSI 35.9.
themes.label: Software: Cash Generation vs Price
themes.narrative: Software is dead money — AI eats SaaS, the sector is being derated for good, and the multiple compression is permanent.
themes.watchFor: Next prints holding revenue growth above 25% with free-cash-flow margin intact confirm the dislocation; a growth guide-down voids it.

themes.counterRead: Rates and credit agree the stress is equity-concentrated, not systemic — the bond market is not pricing a credit event. But the December 8–9 FOMC is the dated test of that calm: a hawkish surprise is the path by which calm credit flips, and the stand-down line (HY OAS above 4%, VIX above 25) is close enough to watch daily.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.95% and the 2-year 4.61%, with the 2s10s curve at +0.34 — not inverted. HY OAS is 3.40, calm and below the 4% stand-down line. VIX closed 16.61, down 20.26% on the day from a 21.15 five-day high. The real 10-year is 2.69%.
themes.label: Credit and Rates Calm
themes.narrative: Hot data means more hikes — the December 8–9 FOMC is flagged HIGH signal strength and the market is pricing the Fed signaling higher rates.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or VIX closing above 25 breaks the calm read; the Dec 8–9 FOMC is the dated test.

watchFor: SMH close versus the $470 Zone 2 floor and $505 ceiling; NVDA versus the $200 Zone 1 floor and the $175–185 Zone 2 band.
VIX closing above 25 (stand-down) versus rolling over from its 21.15 five-day high (confirmation).
HY OAS above 4% breaks the credit-calm leg (now 3.40).
SPX bouncing into the 7,750–7,820 failure zone and stalling, versus holding above its 7,320.35 200-day average.
SMH volume climax above 1.5x its 20-day average with an intraday reversal (now 1.36x, close in 28% of range).
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex: SMH sits inside Zone 2 at $504.27 and NVDA on the Zone 1 floor at $200.13 while revenue is still growing 61.4% year over year. The trigger is either a volume-climax reversal that completes the capitulation tally, or a break below $470 (SMH) and $175 (NVDA) that opens the next leg down.
